subject: Numeracy
title: One more and one less
objectives: Children will find one more and one less than a number to 5.
Children will use a number line to 10.
content: One more, one less, and number lines to 10.
teachingActivities: Act out one more and one less with real objects and children themselves; use a number line to show that one more is the next number and one less is the number before; use stories such as one more child comes to the door; keep numbers to 5 at first.
learnerActivities: Say one more and one less than a number up to 5 and use a number line to 10.
assessment: Observe whether each child says one more and one less than numbers up to 5.
expectedOutcomes: Says one more than a number to 5.
Says one less than a number to 5.
crossCurricular: Physical Development: moving along a line

lessons.title: One more
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find one more than a number up to five.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say which group has more or fewer and match one to one.
lessons.starter: Say "Three children are in the line. One more child joins. How many now?"
teacherActivities: Put three counters down and add one more.
Say "Three and one more is four."
Act out with children in a line.
learnerActivities: Child adds one and says the number.
Children join the line one at a time.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put three counters down and add one more. Children: Children count the new group.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Three and one more is four." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 3. Teacher: Try different starting numbers. Children: Child adds one and says the number.
Step 4. Teacher: Act out with children in a line. Children: Children join the line one at a time.

practical.title: One more game
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise closely. Keep the line of children safe and orderly.

differentiation.support: Use groups of one to three and count each time.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say one more than seven.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is one more than three?
What is one more than five?

expectedOutcomes: Finds one more than a number
lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say one more.
lessons.homeConnection: Add one more spoon to the table and say the number.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find one more than a number up to five" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: One less
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find one less than a number up to five.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say which group has more or fewer and match one to one.
lessons.starter: Say "Four children are on the bus. One child gets off. How many now?"
teacherActivities: Put four counters down and take one away.
Say "Four and one less is three."
Act out with children on a bus of chairs.
learnerActivities: Child takes one away and says the number.
Children get off the bus one at a time.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put four counters down and take one away. Children: Children count what is left.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Four and one less is three." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 3. Teacher: Try different starting numbers. Children: Child takes one away and says the number.
Step 4. Teacher: Act out with children on a bus of chairs. Children: Children get off the bus one at a time.

practical.title: One less game
practical.safety: Use large counters and chairs placed safely. Supervise the bus game closely.

differentiation.support: Use groups of two to four and count each time.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say one less than ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is one less than four?
What is one less than two?

expectedOutcomes: Finds one less than a number
lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say one less.
lessons.homeConnection: Take one spoon away and say the number.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find one less than a number up to five" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The number line
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use a number line to find one more and one less.
successCriteria: Moves forward one for one more
Moves back one for one less
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say which group has more or fewer and match one to one.
lessons.starter: Show a number line on the floor and say "We can walk forward for more and back for less."
teacherActivities: Stand on three and step forward to four.
Step back to two and say "One less."
Let each child stand on a number and step.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Stand on three and step forward to four. Children: Children watch and say four.
Step 2. Teacher: Step back to two and say "One less." Children: Children say one less.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child stand on a number and step. Children: Child steps forward or back.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Where are you now?" Children: Child says the number.

practical.title: Walk the number line
practical.safety: Keep the number line flat and secured so children do not trip. Move one at a time.

differentiation.support: Walk the line holding the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to take two steps forward and say the number.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is one more than six?
What is one less than six?

expectedOutcomes: Uses a number line for one more and less
Says the number after a step
lessons.conclusion: Walk to ten and back to zero together.
lessons.homeConnection: Draw a number line with chalk and step on it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use a number line to find one more and one less" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: More and less stories
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will solve small stories about one more and one less.
successCriteria: Solves a one more or one less story
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say which group has more or fewer and match one to one.
lessons.starter: Tell a story: "Three ducks are in the pond. One more duck comes. How many ducks?"
teacherActivities: Act out the story with toy ducks.
Tell a one less story: "One duck goes away."
Let children tell their own story.
learnerActivities: Child tells a story with toys.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Act out the story with toy ducks. Children: Children count the ducks.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell a one less story: "One duck goes away." Children: Children count what is left.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children tell their own story. Children: Child tells a story with toys.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many now?" Children: Child says the number.

practical.title: Duck stories
steps: Put toy ducks in a pond.
practical.safety: Use large toy animals only and supervise play. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Tell the story with one to three toys.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a story with more than five.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Did we add or take away?

expectedOutcomes: Solves a one more or one less story
lessons.conclusion: Put the animals away and say the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell a number story with toys at bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "solve small stories about one more and one less" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 2 one more and one less check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child finds one more and one less.
successCriteria: Says one more than a number to 5
Says one less than a number to 5
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say which group has more or fewer and match one to one.
lessons.starter: Sing the number song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: one more, one less and number line.
At each station ask "What is one more?" and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: one more, one less and number line. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is one more?" and watch. Children: Child answers with a number.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: One more and less stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep the floor line flat. Use large counters.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use numbers to three.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to say one more and one less than ten.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says one more; says one less; uses a number line; solves a story.

questions.question: What is one more than four?
What is one less than four?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
Finds one more and one less with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep practising one more and one less at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child finds one more and one less" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
